issues.legal_issue: An agreement to sell immovable property that provides for possession to be delivered without requiring execution of a conveyance is chargeable to stamp duty as a conveyance when the agreement contemplates delivery of possession within a stipulated time.
material_facts: The purchasers entered into a written agreement to buy a flat for a stated price, which the agreement said had been paid in the specified manner.
The agreement provided for possession to be delivered by a specified date, subject to payment of amounts due and force majeure.
The agreement did not provide for execution of a conveyance, and it stated that it was not itself a grant or transfer of the property.
The agreement was referred for determination of the property's market value and was treated as chargeable to duty as a conveyance.
issues.conclusion: The agreement fell within Explanation I to Article 25 of Schedule I and was chargeable to stamp duty as a conveyance.
issues.legal_principle: Under Explanation I to Article 25 of Schedule I of the Bombay Stamp Act, 1958, an agreement to sell immovable property is deemed to be a conveyance where possession is transferred before, at, or after execution of the agreement without a conveyance being executed. The Court construed the Explanation to cover an agreement that itself contemplates delivery of possession within a stipulated time without requiring a conveyance. Section 32A applies to such an agreement mutatis mutandis. The Court also considered the provisions of Sections 4 and 11 of the Maharashtra Ownership Flats Act, 1963, but held that the agreement's execution under that Act did not prevent the stamp-duty rule from applying. No earlier cases are relied upon.

rule.if: stamp_duty_review_of_sale_agreement and agreement_for_immovable_sale and possession_delivery_contemplated and possession_not_conditioned_on_conveyance

predicates.stamp_duty_review_of_sale_agreement: The proceeding concerns the stamp-duty treatment of an agreement to sell.
predicates.agreement_for_immovable_sale: The parties made an agreement for the sale of immovable property.
predicates.possession_delivery_contemplated: The agreement provides for possession to be delivered to the purchaser within a specified time or in specified circumstances.
predicates.possession_not_conditioned_on_conveyance: The agreement does not make delivery of possession dependent on execution of a conveyance.

issues.definition: When a stamp-duty proceeding concerns an agreement for the sale of immovable property that contemplates delivery of possession without requiring a conveyance, the agreement is treated as a conveyance for duty.

issues.legal_issue: Stamp duty imposed on an agreement that is deemed to be a conveyance because it provides for sale and possession is a duty on the instrument, not an unconstitutional duty on the underlying transaction.
material_facts: The purchasers argued that the agreement was only a contract for sale and transferred no right, title, or interest, so duty equivalent to conveyance duty would be imposed on the transaction rather than on an instrument.
The agreement stated the sale price and provided for delivery of possession by a specified date, without providing for a later conveyance.
The stamp-duty provision deemed qualifying agreements to be conveyances and applied conveyance duty to them.
issues.conclusion: The Court rejected the challenge, holding that the levy was on the instrument and that the legislature could impose conveyance-equivalent duty on an agreement meeting the statutory conditions even if title had not passed.
issues.legal_principle: Entry 44 of List III of the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution permits the levy of stamp duties on instruments, subject to the constitutional allocation of matters in Entry 91 of List I. Section 3 of the Bombay Stamp Act, 1958 charges instruments within its scope, and Explanation I to Article 25 of Schedule I deems a qualifying agreement to sell to be a conveyance for stamp-duty purposes. The legislature may select such an instrument for conveyance-equivalent duty where the agreement manifests an intention to sell and contemplates delivery of possession, even though title has not passed. No earlier cases are relied upon.

rule.if: stamp_duty_challenge_proceeding and written_sale_agreement and sale_intention_expressed and possession_delivery_contemplated and duty_imposed_on_agreement

predicates.stamp_duty_challenge_proceeding: The proceeding challenges the validity of stamp duty imposed on a written instrument.
predicates.written_sale_agreement: The instrument is a written agreement for the sale of property.
predicates.sale_intention_expressed: The agreement expresses the parties' intention that the property be sold to the purchaser.
predicates.possession_delivery_contemplated: The agreement contemplates delivery of possession to the purchaser.
predicates.duty_imposed_on_agreement: The stamp duty is imposed on the agreement itself by treating it as an instrument in a specified class.

issues.definition: If a challenge concerns duty imposed on a written sale agreement that expresses an intention to sell and contemplates delivery of possession, the levy is a valid duty on the instrument.
